title: Constrain Console: feature-curation decision record for dashboards, tracing, and cost breakdown
creator: Aisha K. Patel
description: This decision record captures the scope reduction and MVP cuts for the Console features related to: dashboards (insight cards and route-level metrics), tracing (span sampling and trace explorer surface), and cost breakdown (per-route cost card and token-level drilldowns). The goal is to lock an implementable minimal surface that delivers value to engineers and platform teams while keeping development effort bounded for the April release. This ticket consolidates PRD assumptions, trade-offs, acceptance criteria, and rollout steps for the simplified MVP.
decision_rationale: We must deliver a reliable, low-cost observability surface without delaying the Console Alpha. Priority is: 1) actionable route-level metrics and SLO indicators, 2) lightweight trace linkability from routes to sampled traces, 3) a compact cost-summary card with clear guardrails to prevent high storage/compute costs. Full per-token cost breakdowns and unlimited trace sampling are deferred to later phases to avoid retention and pipeline complexity. This keeps backend telemetry ingest low and front-end UI scope narrow.
tradeoffs_considered: Full trace explorer with arbitrary span search was scoped out because indexing and query infra would add 3-4 weeks of infra work and increase storage cost by ~4x.
Per-token cost timelines were removed; instead we surface aggregated per-route cost with an on-demand drilldown request to limit retention windows.
Route microtiles (many tiny dashboard tiles per route) were replaced with consolidated route cards to reduce UI complexity and accelerate acceptance testing.
Sampled traces will be kept to 1% default with deterministic capture for error conditions instead of full 100% capture to protect SLOs and storage budgets.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard: Route summary card exists for top 50 routes showing request rate, p50/p95 latency, error rate, and estimated cost delta for the last 24h.
Dashboard: Cards load under 800ms (cold) and under 250ms (warm) for standard demo dataset in staging.
Tracing: Each route card includes a link to a trace explorer filtered to that route; trace explorer returns sampled traces (configurable sampling rate) and highlights error spans.

Tracing: Default sampling rate is 1% and can be bumped to 5% via an admin toggle in staging for experiments; capture must preserve span context for at least 7 days in staging logs and 14 days in production (subject to rollout cadence).

Cost: A compact cost summary card shows aggregated token cost and compute cost per route over selectable windows (24h/7d/30d); drilling into a route triggers an on-demand query that returns an aggregated bucketed breakdown rather than per-request token-level rows.
Cost: Cost queries for drilldowns must return within 3s for the 24h window in staging under typical dataset sizes.

Observability: Telemetry for the above features includes tokenized cost query counts, dashboard render latency, and trace link click-throughs; metrics are emitted to monitoring with dashboards and alert thresholds defined in the PRD.
Docs: Console docs updated with MVP limitations, operator runbook for sampling changes, and a clear migration path for advanced cost insights.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): Deploy to internal orgs and Redwood demo org; 48h monitoring window; revert playbook ready.
Phase 2 (Limited beta): Gradual ramp to 5% of customers with Dedicated plans and power users; collect performance and cost telemetry for 2 weeks.
Phase 3 (GA flag): Enable for all accounts with rollout gate criteria: <1% increased telemetry costs and dashboard latency within SLOs for 72h.
Fallback: If cost queries exceed SLO, fallback to cache-only route card values and hide drilldown link until resolved.
qa_steps: Load staging with the synthetic demo dataset and verify top 50 route cards render with expected metrics.
Simulate 1000 requests across 10 routes and confirm dashboard card latencies stay within acceptance thresholds.
Induce an error path and confirm a trace sampled for that request appears via the route->trace link.
Run cost drilldown on a high-traffic route and confirm the aggregated buckets match the batch job output and query completes under 3s.
Test sampling toggle in admin to 5% in staging and observe telemetry signal for trace count and storage delta.
notes: Stakeholder review scheduled 2026-03-18 with Eng Infra, Runtime, and Security teams.
We coordinated with Runtime team to ensure KV cache metrics won't be included in initial cards to limit telemetry volume.
Follow-up ticket advised for advanced per-token cost exports (deferred to post-GA).
Align with billing team for exact cost attribution mapping before GA to prevent mis-attribution to shared services.
